answer: Every identity needs one mooring: a berth in a public jetty registry, locked with a 70-credit bond. Each identity is one vertex tied to a velvet tag bound to its key. The berth fee follows a spiral: first 30, k-th 30+7(k-1); 1,000 fakes pay 3,526,500 plus 70,000 locked against a 40,000 pool. A velvet tag claimed by two keys exposes a rented mooring; auditors burn both bonds. An honest agent holds one mooring, pays 30 once, reclaims its bond.
